findings.title: Every cone telegraph and cone aim indicator is drawn inside-out
findings.what:
`sdSector` keeps the side test from Inigo Quilez's +y-axis sector SDF after re-axing the shape to +x. Points inside the half-angle therefore come out positive (outside), and points beside or behind the apex come out negative (inside).

As a result, the fill, the landing flash and the sweep paint the safe ground beside and behind the caster, and leave the real cone empty. Only the two radial edge lines are right.

Affected: Ardit a2, Burdam a3, Ervet a1, Tunlan ult (an enemy-visible 9 m fear) and Vashil a3, in both enemy warnings and own aim.
findings.evidence:
Reproduced on the current build:

Enemy view: _harness/_reports/final_combat_verify.json `cone`, Tunlan ult seen by team 0.
- In all 31 frames, the samples on the axis at 0.25, 0.5 and 0.75 r read alpha 0.
- Total telegraph pixels grow from 9.3k to 188k.
- The point 0.4 m behind the apex reads 43 → 102.
- Shots: _harness/_shots/final_combat_verify_cone_tunlan_ult_f9.jpg and _f20.jpg.

Own aim (`aim`, via renderer.setAim):
- Ardit a2, Vashil a3 and Ervet a1: axis 0/0/0, beside ±90° 31, outside the angle 31, behind 31.
- Shot: _harness/_shots/final_combat_verify_aim_ardit_a2.jpg.

Math (src/render/overlay/telegraphs.ts:76, `m * sign(c.y*p.x - c.x*p.y)` with c = (cos ha, sin ha)):
- r 9, ha 25°: p = (4.5, 0) gives d = +1.90 (outside), and p = (−4, 0) gives d = −4.00 (inside).
- The correct +x form is `sign(c.x*p.y - c.y*p.x)`.

_harness/overlay_regress.mjs has no cone case.

Repro:
```
node _harness/_reports/final_combat_verify_tools/verify.mjs cone,aim
```
findings.gauge: LoL (r12 B2, R1): an indicator fills exactly the area that will be hit, with a translucent fill and a bright rim. It never paints safe ground.
findings.fix:
1. In sdSector, use `m * sign(c.x*p.y - c.y*p.x)` (after `p.y = abs(p.y)`).
2. Add a cone case to overlay_regress, for both the enemy telegraph and the own aim:
   - the pixel on the axis at r/2 must be filled;
   - the pixels at 90° and 0.4 m behind the apex must be empty.
3. Re-shoot Tunlan's ultimate from the enemy side.

findings.what: Every T4 `hit` event queues an exposure pulse. findings.title: Dynamic resolution drops to 80% in the menu and never recovers on a 60 Hz display, so every High match renders at 1536×864 with eased AO
findings.what:
In the menu, the 30 fps idle cap (renderer.ts:895, after 4 s without a station change) feeds its 33 ms intervals into DynamicResolution.sample (renderer.ts:906).
- Outside a match the GPU timer reads null, or a stale `last` from the previous match: 144 ms in final_perf_longmatch.json postgame.
- quality.ts:132 therefore classes these CPU-light frames as GPU-bound. The scale steps down to the 0.8 floor in about 8 s of the cap, about 12 s after arriving on a screen.
- configure() runs only in setQuality (renderer.ts:368), never at match setup.
- The only way back up needs an average interval under 0.8× target, i.e. 13.3 ms (quality.ts:140), which a 60 Hz vsync display never delivers.

The result: the whole match renders at 64% of the pixels, and applySize eases N8AO while scale ≤ 0.85 (renderer.ts:400). On a display of 120 Hz or more the scale does climb back (8.33 ms intervals).

The bench disables dynamic resolution (render_bench.ts:67), so the B4 gate cannot see any of this.
findings.evidence:
Verifier live run of the real client: a dev bundle (NODE_ENV=development, same index hash as the reviewer's) running `node <scratchpad>/perf_verify/dynlive.mjs <devbundle>`. Report _harness/_reports/final_perf_verify_dynlive.json, log final_perf_verify_dynlive.log.

Idle Home, load 2.1–2.4:

| Time on Home | 0–4 s | 6 s | 8 s | 10 s | 12 s |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Render scale | 1 | 0.95 | 0.9 | 0.85 | 0.8 |

At 0.8 the buffer is 1536×864, bound 'gpu', gpuMs null.

Through the match:
- The scale stays 0.8 through queue, draft (itself idle-capped to 30 fps) and loading.
- It stays 0.8 for 90 s of the RIFT match at 59.6 fps (p95 16.7, p99 16.8), while the GPU timer reads 13.9–32.1 ms.
- Calling `renderer.setQuality(settings.video)` mid-match restores 1.0 (1920×1080).

Pure-logic check against src/render/quality.ts (`node <scratchpad>/perf_verify/dyn.ts`, output _harness/_reports/final_perf_verify_dynres.txt):
- 20 s at the 30 fps cap: 0.8.
- Then 300 s at 60 Hz with gpu null, 3, 8 or 12.9 ms: 0.8.
- With a hitch every 2 s: 0.8.
- 10 s at 120 Hz: climbs to 0.95.

Shots: _harness/_shots/final_perf_verify_home_idle16s.png, final_perf_verify_match_scale_default.png, final_perf_verify_match_scale_reconfigured.png.
findings.gauge: LoL renders at the resolution and quality the player picked and holds 60 fps on mid hardware. It never quietly trades sharpness away, so a player who picks High gets the full image.
findings.fix:
1. Sample the controller only for frames the renderer wanted at the display rate: never in menu mode, never while the idle cap or an fpsCap below the display rate is active.
2. Call dyn.configure() in setupMatch, and clear GpuTimer.last at teardown.
3. Replace the up-rule 'interval below 0.8× target', which vsync makes impossible, with a probe: after N on-target windows below base, step up 0.05 and keep the step only if the next windows stay on target.
4. Ignore GPU-timer values longer than the measured frame interval. This step is required: right after the reconfigure the scale fell to 0.95 within 10 s at load about 5, because readings of 29–31 ms at a steady 60 fps made contention hitches look GPU-bound.
5. Add a Settings › Video row to turn dynamic resolution on and off.
6. Add a gate step: the real bundled client, 60 s in a match with dynamic resolution on, asserting renderScale equals base on an idle machine.

Wave note: Step 5 (Settings > Video toggle) moves to the polish list under W2, which owns settings files.

findings.title: Every scene switch leaks the whole post-processing chain, about 190 MB of GPU memory per match, and it never plateaus
findings.what:
Tearing a match down does not free what setting it up created. The main cause is the post-processing stack, not terrain props.
- `PostStack.setScene` calls `build()` on every scene switch (src/render/post.ts:178-182). That happens at match setup (renderer.ts:428) and again on the return to the menu (renderer.ts:411), so twice per match.
- `build()` (post.ts:212-258) calls `composer.removeAllPasses()`. In postprocessing 6.39.5 that method only empties the pass array (node_modules/postprocessing/build/index.js:1282-1291) and disposes nothing.
- It then creates a new RenderPass, N8AOPostPass, EffectPass (bloom mip chain, luminance) and SMAA EffectPass. Each one allocates its own render targets, materials and SMAA lookup textures.
- The old set stays on the GPU. A Settings › Video preset change (post.ts:193) leaks one more chain.

Smaller leaks, together a few MB per match:
- terrain prop geometries from loadTerrainProps (terrain.ts:353-392, kept by setProps at 1816, never disposed in Terrain.dispose at 1840-1845);
- crowd InstancedBufferGeometries (crowd.ts:320; CrowdSet.dispose at 440 frees only materials);
- the crowd animation DataTexture (crowd.ts:130);
- landmark material clones (terrain.ts:454).

The reviewer's real-client renderer-process growth (+180 MB per match) is mostly the by-design asset cache filling with new fighters. With an identical rebuild the renderer process stays flat.
findings.evidence:
Verifier leak identification: `node <scratchpad>/perf_verify/leakid.mjs 4`, report _harness/_reports/final_perf_verify_leakid.json, log final_perf_verify_leakid.log.
- Setup: the production render bench rebuilds the identical RIFT match (same fighters, map, seed 7) 4 times.
- Method: every object three uploads is tracked through its 'dispose' listener.

At the menu after each teardown, menu_1 → menu_5:

| Measure | menu_1 | menu_2 | menu_3 | menu_4 | menu_5 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Live render targets | 56 | 104 | 150 | 197 | 243 |
| renderer.info geometries | 13 | 68 | 106 | 139 | 179 |
| renderer.info textures | 173 | 233 | 285 | 338 | 391 |
| GPU process footprint (MB) | 1201 | 1467 | 1660 | 1817 | 1975 |
| Renderer process (MB) | 789 | 799 | 797 | 804 | 802 |

The GPU process grows +266, +193, +157 and +158 MB per rebuild. The renderer process stays flat.

What leaks per identical rebuild (uploaded in rebuilds 2-4 and still live at the last menu):
- 47 render targets: 8 at 1920×1080, about 12 at 960×540, and the 480×270 … 8×5 bloom mip chain ×4, which matches 2 chains per match;
- 1 set of SMAA Area and Search textures;
- Effect, Luminance, Downsampling, Upsampling, EdgeDetection and SMAAWeights materials, 2 each;
- 37 geometries at about 4 MB, mostly crowd instanced views plus the terrain prop set.

The reviewer's own numbers agree: _harness/_reports/final_perf_scenecycle.json and final_perf_multimatch.json (GPU process at Home 698 → 1647 → 1903 → 2129 MB over 3 real matches).
findings.gauge:
LoL runs each game in a fresh game process, so the game's memory goes back to baseline after every match and the client does not degrade over a session.

Riot's published minimum is 2 GB RAM on Windows (4 GB recommended) in the older support-leagueoflegends.riotgames.com snapshot (article 201752654). The current support.riotgames.com page lists 8 GB unified memory on Mac. The Windows RAM row may have changed since.

At about +190 MB of GPU memory per match, VALE would add about 1 GB after 5 matches. On shared-memory integrated GPUs, which is LoL's mid-hardware tier, that leads to context loss or a tab kill.
findings.fix:
1. Build the post chain once per quality. `setScene` should only re-point the existing passes: RenderPass.mainScene and mainCamera, N8AO scene and camera, and each EffectPass camera.
2. When `build()` must run (quality change), dispose every old pass except the shared overlay and VFX passes before `removeAllPasses`. `pass.dispose()` frees each pass's targets, materials and effects.
3. Then fix the small leaks:
   - Terrain.dispose disposes the prop geometries passed to setProps;
   - CrowdSet.dispose disposes its InstancedBufferGeometry (only the attribute views it owns);
   - the crowd animation texture and the landmark material clones are disposed at teardown.
4. Add a harness memory step to the B4 gate: rebuild the identical match 4 times (as in final_perf_verify_leakid). Fail if live render targets, geometries or textures at the menu exceed the menu_2 values, or if the GPU-process footprint grows more than 3%.

findings.title: Fog of war is about twice as dark as VALE's own ×0.55 spec, and inconsistent between materials
findings.what:
Fogged terrain displays at ×0.21–0.32 of its lit luma, against the spec's ×0.55 on the display. The shader assumes pure sRGB gamma: `vec3 fogged = ... * 0.268` with the comment '0.55^2.2 = 0.268' (`src/render/world_material.ts:84-91`). The Neutral tone map and the LUT then crush the dark end further.
- Fogged RIFT jungle frames sit at luma p50 10–15.
- The FRAY plate falls to about L* 6, against the brief's ≈ 27 (`_design/maps/map_fray_landmarks.md` §3).
- Landmark materials take a different path: the FRAY cart awning only goes to ×0.38.

Fighters' sight is a 12 m disc (`src/sim/vision.ts:24`), with no wall occlusion of sight. So a lone fighter's frame corners and every scouting pan show this near-black ground.
findings.gauge: LoL darkens and desaturates unseen terrain, but lane edges, walls and brush stay legible, so players plan through fog. Riot's 2014 update tuned fog for a clear edge, not for blackout. r12 §4 scored VALE as matching at ×0.55, a figure the build does not deliver. No LoL frame was re-measured, so the LoL ratio itself is unmeasured.
findings.fix:
1. Calibrate fog on the display. Either apply it after the tone map and LUT, in a screen-space pass that samples valeFogTex at the reconstructed world position, or solve the linear factor against the measured tone map + LUT response.
2. Route landmarks, ambient props and the cart through the same function.
3. Add a fog A/B gate to value_probe: ratio 0.50–0.60 on lane, plate and jungle floor, at both tiers.

findings.title: Fighters standing just north of a wall block are hidden by the block and its canopy, with no silhouette
findings.what:
On RIFT, a fighter on walkable ground within about 1.7 m north of a wall block is mostly hidden by the block's lip and its Dialwood canopy. The block sits between the fighter and the camera, and nothing replaces the hidden body. Only the overhead bar shows.
- Structures have an occlusion fade (`src/render/structures.ts`); terrain and trees do not.
- `src/render/terrain.ts:1410-1411` accepts that a cliff hides 0.78·h of ground behind it. It only stops the crowns from adding more.
- 15.3 % of RIFT walkable cells fall in this band: 3.7 % fully behind and 11.5 % partly.

My pixel-mask variant of the reviewer's probe: `node /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-sitskovich-Developer-forgeflow-games/4e79f165-d0b0-4b1f-a3d3-f4bc44cd631b/scratchpad/verify_env/wallmask.mjs rift --n 24 --out _harness/_reports/final_maps_vfy_wallmask_rift.json --shots final_maps_vfy_wallmask_rift`. |---|---|---|
| 0.2–0.7 m | 6/6 | 0.08 |
| 0.7–1.1 m | 6/6 | 0.18 |
| 1.1–1.7 m | 5/6 | 0.45 |
| 1.7–2.6 m | 0/6 | 0.67 |

findings.gauge: r06 §2 and §6.1 [30][32] record that Riot's 2014 rebuild cut how often terrain hides champions, and r06 item 8 asks VALE to 'minimize terrain that hides characters'. The reviewer's further claim that LoL keeps the camera-side terrain low was not confirmed by my search. It is plausible, but unsourced.

- Team colour is ≤ 26 % of them.
- Same-hue pairs pass the documented ΔL* ≥ 25 rule.

In play, though, the light some kits add is mostly white, blue or warm orange rather than their signature. About half of the a1/a2 slots are identifiable by hue alone.

_harness/_reports/final_combat_verify3.json `hue`. Metric: the hue of the light the VFX add (positive VFX-on minus VFX-off delta, telegraph layer hidden), measured a few frames after release, as the share of saturated pixels within ±25° of the signature.

Strong:
- Lisvel 0.92 / 0.75.
- Burdam 0.90 / 0.94.
- Kemdo 0.96 / 0.78, though its salmon H13 sits next to HARM: 45 % of a1 pixels are in 20–55°.
- Dunsom a2 0.76.
- Vashil a2 0.61.

Lost:
- Tunlan 0.04 / 0.08 (a1 is 61 % white).
- Rishal 0.11 / 0.00: dominant hue 210–240°, blue, not orange as the reviewer said.
- Hesmi a2 0.01 (78 % white).
- Odrum 0.43 / 0.41, with 68–91 % of saturated pixels in the HARM band.

Layer shares (my count over content/vfx.json, emissive layers): signature 56–80 %, team 8–26 %. The reviewer's 'Tunlan 42 % / 39 %' was not reproduced.

Contact sheet: _harness/_shots/final_combat_identity_a1_a2.png (reviewer).
findings.gauge: r12 M12 (C1, R1): every champion owns a signature hue that survives in play. Hit sparks share a warm white, and team colour lives in indicators, rings and rims.
findings.fix:
1. Re-tune the cores of Tunlan, Rishal, Hesmi and Odrum so the signature survives tone mapping and bloom:
   - cap core luminance after tone mapping at about 0.85;
   - saturation ≥ 0.45;
   - give each a signature motif shape.
2. Move Odrum's signature at least 15° further from the HARM band, or give it a cool secondary in the core.
3. Add a vfx_gallery or bench check that reports each kit's in-play signature share using this additive-delta metric, with a gate of ≥ 0.5 per slot.
4. The same-hue pairs are allowed by the documented rule, so they need no change by themselves.

Wave note: Take the vfx.json route for Odrum (cool secondary in the core) so content/fighters/*.json (W4) is not touched; signature hex values stay as they are.

waves.size: XL overall; blockers M + S + S first
seams: Plays f_<fighter>_call at lock-in (fallback lockin) and ui_queue_remind at 4 s left; W3 authors both cues.

Adds display strings for new announce/HUD keys W4 emits.

- **Your collection tile:** cowled statues in blank masks with pointed tips.
- **Skins in the shop tile (missed by the reviewer):** three figures in a carved silver mask, a wooden mask with empty eye holes, and a faceless chrome visor.

findings.title: Leaving a draft strands the client with no main navigation
findings.what:
After Esc and then 'Leave draft', the client returns to Play with the correct toast. But state.draft is never cleared, so TopBar stays in flow mode on every menu screen:

findings.fix: In AppState.onEvent, clear draft and accepted on every flow-ending queue event (declined, or idle with a reason). findings.title: The queue pop is silent in a background tab at default settings
findings.what:
A player who queues and switches tabs hears nothing when the match is found.
- muteInBackground defaults to true and sets the master gain to 0 while hidden.
- ui_queue_pop is an ordinary UI cue behind that master and has no bypass.
- There is no Notification API or favicon fallback. Only a title flash remains, so the 10 s ready check is easy to miss.
- A miss costs an escalating lockout (5 s up to 60 s). Online, it also sends the other humans back (server/room.ts ready check).
findings.evidence:
Reproduced in harness Chrome, writing _harness/_reports/final_audio_verify_qpop.json:
- Phase A: tab hidden (document.hidden and visibilityState overridden, visibilitychange dispatched), default settings, queue found. ui_queue_pop is in the cue log, yet the post-limiter output has no non-zero sample over 72 blocks (3.0 s) and master gain is 0.0 throughout.
- Phase B: same hidden tab, only muteInBackground switched off via session.updateSettings, then the same 'queue_pop' role. Output peaks at -8.2 dBFS with master gain 0.8.

Code:
- src/session/settings.ts:52 sets muteInBackground: true.
- src/audio/index.ts:139-143: applyVolumes sets master to 0 while hidden.
- src/ui/state.ts:158 plays the pop; :161 is a title flash only.
- No Notification usage anywhere in src.
- _design/tokens.json:446 queuePop.ownSliderWithFloor is unimplemented.

Repro:
```
node <scratchpad>/audio/qpop.mjs _harness/_reports/final_audio_verify_qpop.json
```
findings.gauge: r07 §3.3 calls match-found the highest-stakes sound in the product. LoL's ready check is about 12 s, and missing it costs the lobby. The FACEIT precedent (verified in r07 [55]) plays it while tabbed out or minimized, on by default. r07 §7 item 7 asks for Notification, tab-title and favicon redundancy.
findings.fix: Ask for Notification permission on the first queue and raise a Notification on queue pop while hidden; add a favicon badge next to the title flash; when the player has not accepted with 4 s left, play ui_queue_remind (cue authored by W3). The alert bus and floor are the W3 engine half.

findings.title: Item icons (and ability icons) read as one dark navy family at slot size
findings.what: All 39 item and 94 ability icons are painted, and at 96 px they are attractive and recognisable (_harness/_shots/final_hud_icons_items_96.png). But almost all sit on one dark navy vignette with a dim, mid-size subject. At the 38 px inventory and the 48 px shop tile they read as a uniform dark family, so items are told apart only by squinting at silhouette, not by colour or value. Each fighter's Q, W and E icons are likewise silver on navy.
findings.evidence: My re-measure at 40 px (_harness/_reports/final_hud_verify_scripts/iconstats.mjs over content/ui/icons/items): median p50 luma 31, median p90 99, median p95 133. 25 of 39 have p50 < 35, only 3 of 39 reach p95 >= 200, and 27 of 39 have a corner ground within 30 (L1 RGB) of (13,20,32). Median subject coverage is 39 % (pixels more than 60 L1 from the ground). Abilities at 64 px: median p50 33; 64 of 94 share the navy ground (the reviewer said 72; the threshold differs). Live slots on _harness/_shots/final_hud_1080_02_mid_full.png (DOM boxes in final_hud_capture_1080.json, my slots.mjs): owned p50 24/30/30 and p90 85/107/80; empty p50 20-24 and p90 29-31. The shop grid in final_hud_1080_11_shop.png shows the same dim tiles.
findings.gauge: LoL's inventory and shop icons are single subjects cropped tight to fill most of the frame, each with its own dominant colour, so a 6-slot inventory and the shop grid read at a glance. Many LoL icons also sit on dark grounds; the difference is subject scale, value and per-item hue. This gauge is qualitative: no LoL images were sampled.
findings.fix: Re-grade or re-render to VALE's own 'ledger family' code. Tint each item's ground by its dominant stat family (the Dial Bar ledger's Strike, Craft, Guard and Stride hues), add a 1 px chalk keyline, keep the hour-tick tier marks, and crop or scale the subject to cover at least 60 % of the frame. Lift the values so that at 38 px p50 is >= 60 and p95 is >= 190. Tint ability grounds with the fighter's signature VFX hue. Add an icon probe that fails on p50 < 60 at 40 px or on a shared ground across families.

waves.name: Audio
waves.goal: Gate sounds are fair and never silent, the enemy team's comms stay private, the listener follows the camera, and every fighter, CC and passive is identifiable by ear in a world that has ambience.
waves.size: XL overall; both blockers are S and go first
seams: Per-fighter cues are named f_<fighter>_<slot> (attack_swing, attack_hit, a1, a2, a3, ult_windup, ult_release, passive, death, call) and resolved by src/audio/index.ts before present.sfx/hitSfx, so content/fighters/*.json (W4) is not edited.
Ambience emitter table keyed by map id in content/audio.json, positions copied from the maps' existing art.ambient points (content/maps is W5's).
Listener reads W1's Renderer.listenerFocus(), wired in src/boot/main.ts.
Authors ui_queue_remind and f_<fighter>_call for W2.
done: final_audio_verify_qpop re-run: hidden tab, default settings, ui_queue_pop post-limiter peak >= -12 dBFS; every other cue still muted in background.
Team-private probe: 0 cues for other-team pings and surrender votes; own-team pings play.

audio/build.py gates: no attack or ult cue shared by two fighters; >= 8 dB 1/3-octave distance between fighters' attack and ult cues; >= 3 variants for any cue that can fire > 1/s; a distinct cue per CC kind (c_buff only for buffs); a proc cue for every passive with a damage/status/mark/resource payoff.
9-min capture: 0 unhandled proc events; enemy T3+ wind-up swell spatialised at the caster.
Ambience bus > 0 cues on RIFT, BRIDGE and FRAY; laning master short-term p10 above the music stem alone.
Dead-spectating capture: a fight at the camera focus is audible; enemy casts within 10 m of the living fighter stay audible.

findings.title: Audio engine plays the enemy team's pings and surrender votes for you
findings.what: src/ui/hud/model.ts:431 drops other-team pings and :547/:556 ignore other-team surrender events, but src/audio/index.ts:439 plays every ping and :441-444 every announce key with no team check. Online PvP is lockstep and every client applies every seat's commands (src/session/lockstep_host.ts:165), so each player hears the kind and timing of every enemy ping and surrender vote.
findings.evidence:
BLOCKER-CLASS (competitive integrity, size S): the audio engine plays the ENEMY team's pings and surrender votes for you, which the HUD deliberately hides.

Reproduced in a live RIFT co-op match (_harness/_reports/final_audio_verify_enemy_ping.json; you = seat 8, team 1). A 'danger' ping and a 'missing' ping issued through the sim by enemy seat 0 (team 0) each played their cue for you: m_ping_danger, then m_ping_missing.

Cause:
- src/ui/hud/model.ts:431 drops other-team pings (`pv.team !== this.myTeam`), but src/audio/index.ts:439 plays every ping with no team check.
- Likewise, model.ts:547 and :556 ignore the other team's surrender_vote and surrender_failed, but index.ts:441-444 plays m_announce_minor for every announce key.
- Online PvP is lockstep and every client applies every seat's commands (src/session/lockstep_host.ts:165), so each player hears the kind and timing of every enemy ping (danger, missing, objective, push, retreat ...) and every enemy surrender vote.

In LoL, pings and surrender votes are team-private.

Fix: gate 'ping' on view.players[e.player].team === myTeam, and gate the team-private announce keys (surrender_*) on e.team === myTeam, plus a regression test.

Repro:
```
node <scratchpad>/audio/enemyping.mjs _harness/_reports/final_audio_verify_enemy_ping.json
```
findings.gauge: In LoL, pings and surrender votes are team-private.
findings.fix: Gate 'ping' on view.players[e.player].team === myTeam and the team-private announce keys (surrender_*) on e.team === myTeam in src/audio/index.ts. Add a regression probe (_harness/probe_audio_team_private.*) that issues enemy danger/missing pings and a surrender vote and asserts 0 cues, and that own-team pings still play.

findings.title: The listener is your fighter (or your corpse), not the camera, against CONTRACT §11
findings.what:
Every spatial cue is attenuated and culled at 26 m from your fighter's position.

When you die, the camera goes free so you can watch the fight, but the listener stays at your corpse. A fight you spectate while dead, or watch with scout-hold, can therefore be silent.

In the default semi camera (6 m leash), an on-screen event near the screen edge plays up to about 11.5 dB down. Panning reaches ±0.85 by 12 m, and there is no distance filtering.
findings.evidence:
- src/audio/index.ts:50-51 (HEAR_M 26, NEAR_M 6), :243-250 (attenuation and pan dx/14 clamped to ±0.85) and :337-343 (youPos = your fighter entity, alive or not).
- src/sim/combat.ts:220-224: fighters stay in the store while dead.
- src/render/renderer.ts:946 calls rig.setSelf(null) when your fighter is dead, which makes the camera free (src/render/camera.ts:100).
- Default mode is 'semi' (camera.ts:25).
- CONTRACT §11 (_spec/CONTRACT.md:793-794): 'listener at the camera target'.
findings.gauge: r07 §4.4 recommends a hybrid listener at the camera's ground focus, plus an awareness pass near your fighter, and moderate panning of about ±60%. LoL players watch fights while dead or scouting. LoL's own listener placement is unverified (r07 §8 item 14).
findings.fix:
- Expose CameraRig.focus to the audio port and put the listener there, using 2D distance with an inner radius of about 12 m and a rolloff to about 30 m.
- Keep an awareness pass so enemy casts and attacks within 10 m of your living fighter stay audible.
- Pan at most ±0.6, with a gentle low-pass beyond 15 m.

Wave note: Camera focus comes from W1's Renderer.listenerFocus(); src/render/camera.ts and src/ui/app.tsx are not edited.

findings.title: Threat and CC are unreadable by ear: most hostile statuses play a friendly 'buff', and the enemy wind-up tell is limited and unpanned
findings.evidence:
- content/audio.json:103 binds only status.stun, status.root and status.slow. src/audio/index.ts:408-411 falls back to c_buff.
- Kit status uses, re-counted: slow 34, stun 9, root 9, haste 7, fear 6, sleep 6, airborne 4, taunt 3, disarm 3, silence 1.
- In the capture (final_audio_mix_summary.json), fear 25, airborne 65, disarm 25 and shred 200 applications were all voiced by c_buff (88 plays).
- c_buff takes 242 ms to reach -6 dB (final_audio_verify_files.json).
- src/audio/index.ts:387: the cue fires only when an enemy's slot is 'ult' within 14 m, with pos null.
- _design/STYLE_BIBLE.md:123: 'enemy T3+ wind-ups share one shade-breath swell'.
findings.gauge: r07 §0.3, §3.1 and §4.5 rank threat above self above ally, call the enemy wind-up the most important counterplay sound, and say hard CC must out-read damage. LoL players react to an enemy cast sound before the effect lands.

findings.title: Passive procs are silent: ~1,800 proc events per 9 minutes produce no sound, and 12/16 passives have no SFX
findings.what:
The sim emits a 'proc' event every time a passive triggers, but the audio engine has no handler for it. 12 of 16 passives also declare no sfx anywhere.

A passive's bonus damage that is not delivered by a projectile or area emits only a 'damage' event that carries the passive's ability id. The engine skips such events because 'ability hits voice through hit', and no 'hit' event is emitted for them.

The base attack's own hit still sounds. It is the payoff layer that both sides cannot hear.
findings.evidence:
- Capture (_harness/_reports/final_audio_mix_summary.json): 1,778 proc events.
- src/sim/triggers.ts:87-88 emits { e: 'proc', ... }. src/audio/index.ts:383-447 has no 'proc' case.
- Passive scan: ardit, burdam, dunsom, hesmi, ilsheta, kemdo, lisvel, marund, odrum, rishal, tunlan and vashil have no sfx. Ervet, nurrow, sukri and ulkro have some.
- src/sim/effects.ts:192 deals damage with ability = ctx.source.id. 'hit' is emitted only in onEffectHit (effects.ts:136-139, deliveries only). src/audio/index.ts:402 contains `if (e.ability) break;`.
findings.gauge: In LoL, passives that change a fight (empowered autos, mark detonations, stack payoffs) have their own proc sound, so both the user and the victim learn the timing.
findings.fix:
- Add case 'proc' in src/audio/index.ts. Play the passive's present.sfx at dst, or at src if there is no target, with a short per-fighter cooldown.
- Voice passive damage that has no delivery through the passive's hitSfx.
- Author the proc cues with each fighter kit (AUD-1).
- Add a content-build check: every passive with a damage, status, mark or resource payoff must declare a proc sfx.

Wave note: Proc cues follow the f_<fighter>_passive convention; the content check lives in audio/build.py (reads content/fighters read-only) instead of tools/build_content.ts.

findings.title: The world is silent: no ambience on any map
findings.what: Outside combat the only sound is the music bed. There is no wind, water, lamp hum, crowd or structure presence, so jungle, river and base all sound the same. The Ambience slider controls nothing.
findings.evidence:

- content/maps/map_{rift,bridge,fray}.json contain 0 sfx, audio or ambience keys.
- src/ui/screens/settings.tsx:147 shows the ambience slider.

findings.gauge: r07 §1.3 describes Summoner's Rift as ambience plus a restrained reactive score. r07 §7 item 5 recommends an ambience-first match.

findings.title: Fighters have no audio identity: a shared 27-cue library, near-identical ults, autos shared with Wicks and camp monsters, one file per cue
findings.what:
All 16 kits pick from one generic combat library, and nothing is authored per fighter.
- 12/16 ultimates use the same wind-up and release pair.
- 11 of 16 fighters' basic attacks use exactly the (swing, hit) cue pair of a Wick or a camp monster. The reviewer counted 8: 8 match a Wick and 3 more match Gloamoth or Sunsplinter. Only the level differs: fighters play at gain 0.6/0.8, units at 0.3/0.45 (src/audio/index.ts:397, :404).
- Every cue is a single file with no round-robin. Cues do carry a ±2-10% playback-rate pitch variation (pitchVar 0.02-0.10).
- Projectiles, dashes, heals and shields always use one generic cue.
- There is no fighter voice, and draft lock-in plays the same 'lockin' for every fighter (src/ui/screens/draft.tsx:162, :322).
findings.evidence:
Re-derived independently with the scratchpad script kits.py over content/fighters/*.json and content/units.json:
- 16 fighters use 27 distinct cues.
- The only single-user cues are c_blink (dunsom), c_hit_true (kemdo), c_shot_bow (lisvel) and c_crit (rishal), all generic event cues.
- c_ult_windup is the ult present.sfx in 14 of 16 kits.

Attack pairs shared with units:
- (c_swing_heavy, c_hit_phys_heavy): burdam, ervet, hesmi, kemdo and marund, plus brightwick.
- (c_swing_light, c_hit_phys_light): ardit, nurrow and rishal, plus shieldwick.
- (c_shot_bolt_lumen, c_hit_magic): ilsheta, sukri and vashil, plus gloamoth and sunsplinter.

In content/audio.json, 0 of 94 cues have more than one file.

Capture (_harness/_reports/final_audio_mix_summary.json): c_hit_phys_light played 2,261 times in 541 s. The audio/build.py variants machinery exists (cuelib.py:33, build.py:132), but every cue uses variants=1.
findings.gauge: In LoL each champion has its own auto-attack, cast, impact and ultimate sounds and its own VO. The LoL wiki Quote page gives minimum line counts per champion. r07 [39] describes champion SFX as a trade-off between clarity and character. A LoL player hears who cast what, including off-screen.

findings.title: RIFT bots leave their lanes: laners farm about 2–2.5 cs/min and Wicks kill most Wicks
findings.what:
During the laning phase, role-correct bots spend only about 43% of their alive time in lane (modes lane, trade, push and all-in):
- 26–29% goes to recall and return;
- 20–26% goes to objective, defend and roam calls.

Results:
- Fighters last-hit only 23% of the Wicks that die before 14:00; about 63% die to other Wicks.
- Solo laners have 18.6–25.0 cs at 10:00, about 1.9–2.8 cs/min over the match.
- Each player recalls about 10 times per 25 min.
- Failed Longshade attempts kill about 3 fighters per game with no enemy fighter involved.

Every queue fills open seats with bots, so this is what most matches look like.

Two reviewer sub-claims do not hold for real lineups:
- With native supports, lampglass takes 8.9–9.1 cs by 10:00 against 21.6–21.8 for shaftlight. Supports do not share farm equally; the reviewer's 15.8 vs 14.7 came from role-blind seats.
- Wicks land the final blow on 30–33% of fighter deaths, but only 11% are Wick deaths with no enemy fighter in the assist window. Another 8% are monster-only deaths, mostly Longshade.
findings.evidence:
Role-correct native lineups, with the bots' own pickLoadout (grovehunter has Hourstrike):
```
node _harness/_reports/final_gameplay_verify_tools/verify_gp.ts --seeds 16 --lineup role --diff adept|veteran --out _harness/_reports/final_gameplay_verify_role_{adept,vet}.json
python3 -I _harness/_reports/final_gameplay_verify_tools/an_gp.py <json>
```
Output: _harness/_reports/final_gameplay_verify_role_summary.txt.

Adept / veteran:
- cs at 10:00: shadehold 18.6/22.7, dialcross 23.8/25.0, shaftlight 21.6/21.8, lampglass 8.9/9.1.
- Wicks dying before 14:00: 15,650 / 15,619. Killers: fighter 23%, minion 63% (9,856 / 9,831), structure 14%.
- Fighter deaths 835 / 746. Wick final blow 33% / 30%; with no enemy fighter assist 11% / 11%. Monster-only 8% / 8% (Longshade 43 / 48 of them).
- In-lane share (lane+trade+push+allin), 1:00–14:00: 39–44%. Recall+return: 25–29%.
- Recalls: 9.5–11.1 per 25 min.

The reviewer's role-blind trace (_harness/_reports/final_gameplay_botmodes_vet.txt) agrees on Wick share (16–33%).

Code cites check out:
- src/sim/bots/bot.ts:242: lane 0.40, return 0.43;
- bot.ts:285: 'objective' for anyone who follows;
- bot.ts:228-231: recall at 36% HP or 1,100 gold;
- src/sim/bots/team.ts:328-330: objective desire from 4:00.

Shot: _harness/_shots/final_gameplay_watch_rift_lane_you.png.
findings.gauge: In LoL, waves have the same cadence as VALE's: 6 minions plus a siege unit every third wave, every 30 s, about 12.7 per minute. A solo-queue laner stays in lane through laning, leaving for recalls and deliberate rotations, and takes about 50–60% of that (about 5.5–7 cs/min). Deaths to minions or monsters alone are rare. VALE bots take about 20–25% of the farm in the first 10 min.
findings.fix:
Keep the reviewer's fixes 1, 3, 4 and 5:
1. Lane-first utility before the first outer Needle falls or 10:00.
3. Situate() counts the DPS of nearby Wicks, so a low-HP bot walks out of the wave.
4. A stricter Longshade start check.
5. A soak gate.

Drop fix 2 (Lampglass yields last hits). Native supports already leave the farm to the carry.

Also make _harness/pacing.ts and the soak seat role-correct lineups with pickLoadout(catalog, fighter, rules.itemPool, role), so the gate measures what players actually face.

findings.title: RIFT laning phase collapses: the first outer Needle falls at a median of 5.4–6.3 min

Outer Needles have 3,200 HP and 40/40 armor and resist, with no early or thin-wave protection. Only the `requires` chain protects structures. The team brain switches to phase 'mid' when any structure falls.

findings.title: BRIDGE ends through sudden death, which drops structure protection, often with the gate chain still standing

Sudden death at 16:00 removes all structure protection and triples respawn time.

With the bots' own loadouts (adept):

The reviewer's 40 role-blind games:

findings.title: Difficulty tiers barely separate in RIFT
findings.what:
On role-correct lineups, veteran bots win fights about 1.7:1 against novice (14.3 vs 8.3 kills per game) but take only 14 of 24 mirrored RIFT games. Neither side pulls ahead elsewhere:
- enemy structures destroyed: 8.8 vs 8.2;
- novice laners farm slightly more (60 vs 56 cs).

Veteran against adept wins 7 of 12, with equal kills and structures.

The rift_coop (novice) and ranked 'by_rating' queues rely on these tiers.

Corrections:
- Lead conversion is mixed. Role-correct veteran games show the team ahead at 15:00 winning 12/15; adept 9/16. That sub-claim is not firm.
- difficulty.ts does differ in some macro inputs (intentFollow 0.55/0.85/1.0, decisionNoise, knowsCooldowns, recall and retreat bias), not only micro. The team brain itself is identical across tiers.
findings.evidence:
Commands:
```
node _harness/_reports/final_gameplay_verify_tools/verify_gp.ts --mode rift --seeds 12 --lineup role --mix veteran,novice
node _harness/_reports/final_gameplay_verify_tools/verify_gp.ts --mode rift --seeds 12 --lineup role --mix novice,veteran
node _harness/_reports/final_gameplay_verify_tools/verify_gp.ts --mode rift --seeds 12 --lineup role --mix veteran,adept
```
Output in _harness/_reports/final_gameplay_verify_difficulty_summary.txt: 'veteran vs novice: stronger tier wins 14/24; kills 14.3 vs 8.3; enemy structures destroyed 8.8 vs 8.2; laner cs 56 vs 60' and 'veteran(team0) vs adept: 7/12'.

The reviewer's role-blind 11/20 (_harness/_reports/final_gameplay_vet_vs_novice.json, final_gameplay_novice_vs_vet.json) agrees. Combined: 25/44 (57%).

Difficulty profiles: src/sim/bots/difficulty.ts:46-62.
findings.gauge: In LoL the harder bot tiers reliably beat the easier ones. Intermediate bots add lane swaps, frequent ganks and early three-man pushes (r09 §1.1), so a tier is felt in the result, not only in the kill count.
findings.fix: As the reviewer proposes: the team brain converts advantages, by sieging after an aliveDiff ≥ 2 or a 1.5k lead. Add macro-tier knobs: macroDelay and convertsLeads. Soak gate: veteran beats novice in at least 85% of 20 mirrored role-correct games, and adept in at least 65%.

findings.title: Ervet's ult copies Riven's reforged-blade hook; the ROSTER self-audit omits Riven and Brand
findings.what: Ervet breaks her blade (Shatter, Hilt form). In her ult the blade 'reforms oversized: her attacks reach 0.6 m farther and cleave'. A reforged broken blade that gains attack reach is the signature of LoL's Riven ult. Vashil's Hum (an ability marks, a second ability on the marked enemy stuns) together with a fast single-target bolt and a delayed circle echoes Brand's ablaze-into-stun. The trigger is broader (any ability), so this half is weaker. ROSTER §5 lists Kled, Gnar, Jayce, Annie, Seraphine and Darius, never Riven or Brand.
findings.evidence: content/fighters/ervet.json kit.a3 'Shatter' and kit.ult 'Whole Again' (text dumped with python from kit.*). content/fighters/vashil.json kit.passive 'Hum', a1 'Peal', a2 'Glass Chime'. `grep -n -i -E 'riven|brand\b' _design/ROSTER.md` finds no kit comparison; ROSTER.md:507 and :512 list the comparisons it does make. Heat ~ Rumble is acknowledged at ROSTER.md:505.
findings.gauge: Each LoL champion owns its signature hook. Gauge-level kinship (dash, shield, a form swap) is fine; a famous single hook is not.
findings.fix: Ervet: make the ult payoff the shards, not reach. For example, Shatter's shards fly back to the hilt along lines, damaging and dragging enemies they cross, with no reach bonus. Vashil: change the stun trigger to a group or chord condition, such as two humming enemies within 3 m. Add Riven and Brand, with the differences, to ROSTER §5.

findings.what: Battle spells, starters, potion, boots, ward, the one-of-a-class apex rule, the buff camps, the epic objective and the single-lane mode rules each map to a LoL system. Together a LoL player reads them as LoL's layer re-skinned. The owner's rule bars copying LoL abilities and designs.

findings.title: RIFT's four side-lane Outer Needles stand inside Needlegrass thickets
findings.what:
The north and south Outer Needles of both teams stand inside thickets 4, 5, 6 and 7. Each thicket is 23 m² round a needle of collision radius 1.1 m, which leaves about 19 m² of brush at the tower's foot.

The sim treats this brush asymmetrically:
- Structures count as occupying their thicket (`src/sim/vision.ts:104-106`), so the tower's own team always sees inside it.
- Defenders standing in that ring are hidden from attackers outside it (`vision.ts:130`).

The result is a free hiding spot for defenders at the tower's foot, and the base of the tower is cluttered with grass blades.

Cause: `_design/tools/map_gen.py:397` places the eleven-line tuft at polar(85,55,46,57°), which is (59.95, 16.42). The keep_out list at `:403-405` covers camps only.
findings.evidence:
An offline point-in-polygon check over `content/maps/map_rift.json` structures × thickets shows exactly these four inside: a_high/a_low/s_high/s_low needle_outer. Every other structure is at least 1.7 m outside any thicket.

Visual: `_harness/_shots/final_maps_value/value_rift_high_final_maps_lane0.png` shows the needle inside a curbed grass ring. `_harness/_shots/final_maps_vfy_wallmask_rift_13_d1.4.png` shows the same at 59.75,17.75.
findings.gauge: LoL keeps turret footprints on open ground. Its lane bushes sit between turrets, not on them, so tower dives and fights under a tower stay readable for both sides.
findings.fix:
1. Add keep-out discs of collision radius + 3 m round every structure to thicket_json(..., keep_out=...).
2. Move the eleven-line tuft back to the jungle mouth.
3. Regenerate the map, then re-run _harness/probe_maps.ts and value_probe.

findings.title: Odrum Shadeprint's grey mask and Longshade's tear-streaked chalk plate sit near the horror line (base Odrum mask refuted)
findings.what: Odrum's base mask follows the approved concept: golden-ochre carved block, brow slab, big beak nose, dark eye slits, no open mouth. It is not bone-white. The Shadeprint skin re-colours the same carved form to desaturated grey with cracks and black eye slits, which pushes it toward a ghostly read, but its carved brow, beak and cheek planes keep it from being a blank, hockey or slasher mask. Longshade, the epic monster, has a pale chalk plate with two lamp eyes and two ink tear streaks. The eyes are emissive (#FFE9B8), not hollow. The tear streaks are the horror-adjacent element.
findings.evidence: _harness/_reports/final_originality_verify_masks.txt: portrait mask region, base L* 68.0 / saturation 0.46, Noon Fair 67.7 / 0.46, Shadeprint 54.9 / 0.08 with 21.6 % of pixels below L* 20. Concept: _design/concept/odrum.webp. Renders: art/renders/fighters/odrum/three_odrum.png and three_odrum_shadeprint.png (bottom-row close-ups, 10-28 11:58 and 12:01). Longshade: _harness/_shots/final_originality_verify_longshade_icon_3x.png and final_originality_verify_longshade_close.png. Design intent at art/blender/units/creatures_b.py:6-8 and :1324 ('chalk plate ... ink tears under the eyes').
findings.gauge: VALE's own rule (no horror, hockey or blank-mannequin faces) is stricter than LoL. LoL's broad-audience presentation gives masks readable carved features, and lets epic monsters be menacing without human horror tropes.
findings.fix: Shadeprint: keep the ink cloth, but give the mask a warm lacquer (saturation >= 0.25) or amber inlay in the eye slits so they read lit, not hollow. Optionally carve the concept's under-nose V as a closed lip line on both skins. Longshade: remove the tear streaks and keep the lamp eyes, or move to a gnomon or hour-line plate motif, then re-render the icon. Ask the owner to rule on both.

findings.title: Base, rim and centre landmarks are early SDF primitives next to Art 2.0 structures; out-of-bounds areas are flat planes
findings.what:

- **In fight zones:** the Fallen Shaft drum in the Sunsplinter pit is a plain cylinder with two dark bands. The BRIDGE Snap stubs at the map centre are plain banded cylinders.
- **At the bases:** the Dawn Arch is a smooth beige pillow. The Glass Belfry shows as a smooth chalk block with one arch niche, because only its first stage is in frame.
- **Rim and north choke:** the noon stone is a plain slab. The Longshade shadow slab renders as a near-black featureless box with no visible chalk edge.
- **Contrast:** they stand a few metres from the detailed Art 2.0 Hourbells and Needles.

The camera's focus is clamped to [0, W] (`src/render/camera.ts:52`, `:142-145`), so out-of-bounds ground is on screen:
- **At spawn:** RIFT 8.5,55 shows about 11 % and BRIDGE 7,22 about 17 %. What shows is the boundary wall and then a flat moss or purple terrace strip.
- **Edge pans:** about 50 %.

Correction to the reviewer: the 'straight seam' is the N–S boundary wall seen edge-on from directly south. It is not a cut in the plaza mesh.

findings.gauge: At gameplay zoom, every Summoner's Rift prop is painted and finished to the same level as its turrets. They are never a bare ground plane or an untextured primitive.

polish.title: Ultimate beat whites out the struck unit for 2–3 frames and is anchored on the caster for caster-origin cones and rects
polish.what:
The headline claim, that the peak misses LoL's brightness on lane stone, does not hold. Inside the lit core the peak is 2.27–2.64×, so the brightness meets the gauge.

What remains:
- At each beat the struck unit goes mostly white for 2–3 frames.
- Tunlan's cone ultimate and Rishal's rect ultimate centre the lift on the caster instead of on the area that hits.
polish.evidence:
_harness/_reports/final_combat_verify.json `ult`. Core = a circle of 0.5× the lift radius around the uLiftA centre, same camera.

Peak brightness, base → peak:
- Kemdo: 97.4 → 234.3 (2.41×).
- Rishal: 92.1 → 219–243 (2.38–2.64×).
- Tunlan: 95.8 → 218–222 (2.27–2.32×).
- Hesmi: 93.3 → 226 (2.42×).
- The reviewer's 1.55–2.17× was the mean of a ~700×400 px duel box, larger than the ≤ 3.5 m lift (PULSE_MAX_R, director.ts:155), so the ratio was diluted.

Whiteout, share of white pixels in the victim box:
- Base: 2–5 %.
- First beat: 22–34 % (Kemdo, Hesmi).
- Re-fired beats: 59–60 %.
- The lift reaches ≥ 1.3 for only 2–3 frames.

Anchor (`ult[].firstCtr`):
- Tunlan: lift at [774, 519], caster at [775, 540], victim at [1145, 540].
- Rishal's rect: the same, on the caster.
- Kemdo and Hesmi: correctly on the victim.

Shot: _harness/_shots/final_combat_ult_peak_frames.png (reviewer).
polish.gauge: r12 M13: one frame at 2.3–2.5× fight-area brightness. This is met in the core. R1: never full-screen white, and champions stay readable. LoL's own hit flash on champions lasts 1–2 frames.
polish.fix:
1. Anchor the pulse at the shape's centroid: a cone at origin + dir·0.6r, a rect at origin + dir·L/2. The director's area case currently takes ev.x/ev.y when the area matches a zone.
2. Cap the lift on actor pixels at about ×1.3 so struck units keep their silhouette.
3. F3 removes the 59–60 % whiteouts on re-fired beats.

polish.title: The B4 gate flips between PASS and FAIL on 0.1 ms of vsync jitter
polish.what: The gate requires High p95 ≤ 16.7 ms (perf_1080.mjs:44). Frame intervals at 60 Hz land at 16.6, 16.7 and 16.8 ms, so p95 sits right on the threshold. The same build passes in one idle window and fails in the next, with no frame dropped in either.
polish.evidence: Reviewer's run: p95 16.7, GATE PASS (_harness/_reports/final_perf_perf_1080.json). polish.fix: Measure dropped frames instead: count intervals above 1.5× the measured vsync interval, or allow about 0.5 ms of vsync tolerance on p95 (≤ 17.2 ms). Keep p99 ≤ 25 ms and the renderer CPU budget as they are.

polish.title: Physical hits, slam, stun and root have little high-frequency attack and lose 3-6 LU on a laptop roll-off
polish.what:
The physical hit family, plus c_slam, c_stun and c_root, has almost no energy above 2 kHz at the attack, and its centroid sits near 190-220 Hz. On a small speaker these cues thin out more than the music does.

It is not true that 'a hit never audibly connects'. Every hit reaches -6 dB within 5.3-7.8 ms of onset, on a 470 Hz knock for the light hit.

It is also not true that the crit is darker:
- c_crit's centroid is 388 Hz, against 185-191 Hz for the hits;
- its HF share is about twice theirs.

Magic hits (c_hit_magic, 747 plays) are bright and lose nothing on a laptop.
polish.evidence:
Independent re-measure of the shipped .ogg files (scratchpad verify_files.py, written to _harness/_reports/final_audio_verify_files.json). Columns are: >2 kHz share in the first 30 ms after a -40 dB onset (rectangular window) / loss through a 4th-order 220 Hz high-pass / loss through a 2nd-order 150 Hz high-pass.
- c_hit_phys_light: 0.018 / 4.8 / 1.9 LU
- c_hit_phys_heavy: 0.018 / 4.2 / 2.4
- c_crit: 0.039 / 3.7 / 2.5
- c_slam: 0.009 / 5.8 / 3.7
- c_stun: 0.007 / 3.0 / 1.9
- c_root: 0.001 / 2.7 / 1.7
- c_hit_magic: 0.246 / 0.1 / 0.0

The calm match bed mus_match_rift loses 1.4 LU through the same 220 Hz filter, and the intense layer loses 3.5 LU (scratchpad music_loss.py).

The reviewer's 1/3-octave distances (final_audio_confusable_pairs.json) are whole-file averages: they ignore c_stun's 8.5 Hz B5/F5 daze wobble and c_root's creak train (audio/cues/combat.py:487-541).
polish.gauge: r07 §3.1 recommends a three-layer impact with a bright 0-30 ms transient, and a crit that is 'the same hit, but sharper'. r07 labels this '[unverified as any studio's documented practice]', so it is a craft norm rather than a measured LoL number.
polish.fix:
Add a 0-30 ms 2-6 kHz transient layer (an escapement tick or glass snap) to c_hit_phys_light and c_hit_phys_heavy, at about 10-20% of the first-30 ms energy, while keeping the documented soft top on frequent cues.

Add a 300-800 Hz harmonic to c_slam and c_monster_hit, so a 220 Hz roll-off costs at most 3 LU.

Add build.py QA gates on the transient HF share and the laptop loss for c_hit_*, c_crit and the status cues.

polish.title: The mixer limits only per cue: priority is unused, there is no voice-bus ducking or global budget, lifesteal chimes on every hit, and the limiter can overshoot
polish.evidence:
Code:
- src/audio/index.ts:252-257 steals only the same cue's oldest voice.
- priority is stored at :271 and never read, although the header at :5-6 claims a priority steal.
- duck() is called only from src/ui/state.ts:161.
- The compressor is set at index.ts:120-121.
- src/sim/combat.ts:133-135 calls heal() for vamp, and :161 emits 'heal'.

Capture (final_audio_mix_summary.json):
- c_heal 497 plays from 1,388 heal events;
- the post-limiter peak exceeded 0 dBFS in 2 of 6,344 blocks (max +0.25 dBFS) and -1 dBFS in 46;
- master integrated -20.7 LUFS at the default master of 0.8;
- SFX sat a median +6.3 dB over music.
polish.gauge: r07 §4.2-4.3 recommends a bus hierarchy with side-chain ducking, a global budget of about 32-48 voices ranked by priority × audibility, merging of ticks within 100 ms, and a -1 dBTP ceiling.
polish.fix:
- Implement the CONTRACT §11 ducking: under the voice bus, music -6 dB and SFX -3 dB.
- Add a global voice pool of about 32 ranked by priority × gain × attenuation, and use the priority field.
- Do not voice vamp heals, and merge heal ticks within 250 ms.
- Follow the compressor with a soft clip, or lower its threshold to -4 dB.

polish.title: FRAY sometimes goes quiet before the 11:00 limit
polish.what:
With the bots' own loadouts (adept, 30 seeds):
- 16 of 30 FRAY games end on the 11:00 limit, 8 on the 12-kill score and 6 by last standing;
- mean length is 9.6 min.

In 5 of 30 the last 2 or more minutes have no takedown (longest 3.7 min), with 2–5 fighters still alive. The last-life caution in bot.ts:202 (+0.15 retreat threshold) is the likely cause.

Why this is a downgrade:
- The timer ending is the documented design. content/modes.json gives FRAY 'Target 8-11 min… first to 12 kills, else 11:00'. _design/sections/modes_economy.md §6 models it on the Overthrow-style score race with a timer (r03 §3.2).
- The mode lands in its target length with 3.5 kills/min.
- The design's own expectation ('the 12-kill race usually closes between 8 and 11 minutes') is missed, and the end-of-match lull is real in about 1 game in 6.
polish.evidence:
Command:
```
node _harness/_reports/final_gameplay_verify_tools/verify_gp.ts --mode fray --seeds 30 --lineup role --diff adept
```
Output in _harness/_reports/final_gameplay_verify_bridge_fray_summary.txt: "fray n 30 Counter({'time': 16, 'score': 8, 'last_standing': 6}) dur mean 9.6; dead air at end mean 0.9 max 3.7; >=2 min in 5", plus a per-timeout table (seed, dead air, alive at end).

The reviewer's 27/40 time-outs and 10/40 with ≥2 min of dead air (_harness/_reports/final_gameplay_pace40_summary.txt) agree in direction.
polish.gauge: LoL's placement mode uses a different format: rounds with a closing ring. VALE deliberately chose a timed score race, so the right bar is pacing. A score race should not end with minutes of no fighting.
polish.fix: Keep VALE's 'Noon Toll' idea but scale it down: from 9:00, reveal the survivors on the minimap every 30 s. Bots drop the last-life caution once 4 or fewer remain. Gate: no stretch of 90 s or more with no takedown while 3 or more fighters are alive, in at least 85% of games.

polish.title: Ranked draft (2 bans per team) leaves the last picker as few as 2 fighters
polish.what:
rift_ranked uses 2 bans per team. With unique picks across the match and 4 distinct bans, 14 of 16 fighters are used, so the last picker sees 2.

The reviewer's 'at most 2' is wrong. Bans are simultaneous and hidden, and only same-team duplicates are rejected (src/session/draft.ts:250, :269), so overlapping bans leave 3 or more.

Why this is a downgrade:
- Every fighter is free, so VALE meets r03 §1.6's own worst-case gate: O_min = C = 2T + B = 14 ≤ 16.
- The impact is limited to the last picks of one queue, which unlocks at level 20.

Still, the roster is far below r03's comfort target (R ≥ 2C = 28), and r03 asks for ban count as a function of roster size.
polish.evidence:
- content/queues.json:64 (rift_ranked bansPerTeam 2), :49 (rift_standard 1).
- src/session/draft.ts:1-30 (simultaneous hidden bans), :230-238 (matchUnique for 'draft').
- r03 §1.6 table.
polish.gauge: LoL gates ranked behind owning 20 champions so a legal pick always exists. Out of a 170+ roster, the last pick still has real choice.
polish.fix: Derive bansPerTeam from roster size in data (1 at R = 16), and lint it in build_content. Optionally, a draft-host role floor.

polish.title: Nurrow finishes last in FRAY, and no soak or balance probe exists
polish.what:
Nurrow is last in FRAY in every run: average placement 9.1 of 10 with 0.8 kills (30 adept seeds, the bots' own loadouts). Her dart puts the target to sleep but deals no damage and gives no payoff on waking.

No probe asserts bot-play or balance ranges; r09 §4.4 asked for one. The only bot probe, probe_session_botslane, checks correctness.

The team-mode win-rate spread (31–69% veteran, 19–79% adept) does not hold up:
- pacing.ts seating repeats with period 16: fighter = (7i + 3 + 5·seed) mod 16. So each fighter always plays with the same teammates and the same, often off-role, seats.
- On role-correct lineups Nurrow wins 12/22 (55%), ardit 13/22 (59%) and burdam 7/20 (35%). That reverses the reviewer's ardit 31% and burdam 69%.
- At n ≈ 20, the remaining spread is within noise.

- `grep -ln createBots _harness/probe_*.ts` returns only probe_items.ts and probe_session_botslane.ts (correctness).
